title: Delegated Access Timing & Proof-of-Change (RBAC v2)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures design notes and a proposed rollout for delegated access semantics in RBAC v2, with emphasis on timing guarantees, cryptographic proof-of-change for entitlement transitions, and how we export this evidence to SIEM and downstream audit pipelines. It is intentionally pragmatic — the goal is an incremental migration that preserves forensic fidelity while keeping latency and cost reasonable.

Background / context (short):
- RBAC v1 baked coarse role assignments; RBAC v2 moves to attribute-anchored grants, session-scoped assertions, and explicit delegation.
- Several customers require provable audit trails showing exactly who requested, approved, and exercised delegated privileges (finance, healthcare).
- Existing SIEM exports are tokenized and lose linkage between the event that changed an entitlement and the subsequent access events.

High-level goals:
1) Provide low-latency delegation flows for common paths (service-account delegation, human->service, human->human short-lived grants).
2) Attach a compact, verifiable "proof-of-change" blob to entitlement-change events (signed digest + metadata) that can be referenced by access logs and SIEM.
3) Ensure audit schema is deterministic and easy to index in Splunk/Elastic / Snowflake.
4) Automate evidence collection and sampling with retention-aware exports to reduce storage cost.

Non-goals:
- We are not building a full PKI for users. We will leverage existing KMS/HSM for signing keys.
- This doc does not define the UI for delegation (product team owns UX).

Main concepts introduced:
- Delegation token: a short-lived assertion object (opaque JSON) describing a delegated grant (who delegated, who received, scope, expiry, constraints).
- Proof-of-change (PoC): a signed metadata envelope that records an entitlement mutation (create/update/revoke) including pre/post snapshots (IDs only), an action timestamp, and an operator id.
- Session assertion: the runtime representation attached to requests referencing a delegation token and optionally PoC id.

Data model (audit / evidence):
- entitlement_change event (primary mutation event):
  - id: uuid
  - op: create | update | revoke
  - subject_id: principal that receives the entitlement
  - actor_id: principal that triggered the change (could be system, user, automation)
  - resource: canonical resource id (model endpoint, dataset, console-route)
  - permission: canonical permission string (e.g., inference:invoke:write)
  - scope: ephemeral attributes (time-window, allowed_ips) as list of tags
  - previous_snapshot_refs: list of entitlement ids (zero or one in most cases)
  - poc_ref: proof_of_change_id (links to PoC envelope)
  - signed_digest: base64(signature over canonicalized-event)
  - timestamp_utc: iso8601
  - region: region code (us-west1)

- proof_of_change (PoC) envelope (stored as separate artifact and exported to evidence store):
  - id: uuid
  - change_event_ref: entitlement_change.id
  - canonical_hash: sha256 of canonicalized payload (hex)
  - signer_kid: key-id (KMS)
  - signature: base64
  - bundle_meta: freeform tags (jira, deployment-id)
  - retention_tier: hot|warm|cold
  - created_at: iso8601

- access_event (for request-level logs):
  - id: uuid
  - request_id: tracing id
  - principal_id: who made request
  - resource, operation, permission_required
  - delegation_token_ref: optional (delegation token id if used)
  - related_poc_ref: optional (points to PoC showing the entitlement enabling this access)
  - result: success | denied | error
  - reason: freeform short code
  - timestamp_utc: iso8601

Schema design notes / indexing considerations:
- Avoid nesting large snapshots inside the primary event. Use refs to PoC artifacts stored separately. This keeps index size small and allows materialized joins in the warehouse when needed.
- Ensure top-level fields used for filtering in SIEM (actor_id, principal_id, resource, permission, region, timestamp) are always present and fixed-name.
- Canonicalize event JSON using stable key ordering and UTF-8 normalization before hashing/signing. Provide a library (python/go/ts) to reproduce canonicalization.

Proof signing and KMS usage:
- Use centralized signing key per environment (prod / staging / dev) managed in HSM/KMS. Keys rotate quarterly.
- PoC signing flow: after change is committed in entitlements store (transactional), enqueue PoC job which builds canonical payload, requests KMS sign, persists PoC artifact, update change_event.poc_ref and change_event.signed_digest atomically (or via compensating transactions if async).
- For low-latency flows where customer expects sub-200ms, we allow an async signing fallback: the change_event is written with "signature_pending" status and PoC finalized within a bounded window (recommended 5s for hosted tier). Production monitoring must alert on backlog.

Evidence automation and sampling strategy:
- Full capture for: admin-level changes, cross-tenant changes, delegation to highly privileged roles, and any reassignments of SLAs.
- Probabilistic sampling for low-risk events (read-only grants, routine service-account rotations) — sample rate configurable per team.
- Always capture a 24-hour window of full events for any tenant with active investigation flag.
- Export batches to evidence store (S3) compressed (ndjson.gz) with manifest files listing PoC ids. Manifests are signed.
- Retention tiers: hot (30d), warm (1yr), cold (7yr) — copy lifecycle managed by retention_tier in PoC envelope.

SIEM export mapping (suggested column set for Elastic/Splunk ingestion):
- event_type, event_id, timestamp_utc, actor_id, principal_id, resource, permission, op, result, poc_ref, signed_digest, region, retention_tier, sample_flag, manifest_id
- Provide transformation library that flattens lists into pipe-delimited strings for simple ingestion.

Rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 - experiments (2 weeks)
- Build PoC signing pipeline behind feature flag; instrument internal tenant only.
- Validate canonicalization library across languages.
- Spike SIEM ingestion for PoC references only (not full PoC payload).
Owners: Maya, Evan. Tickets: SEC-2147.

Phase 1 - canary (4 wks)
- Narrow canary: 5 internal teams + 2 small customers opt-in.
- Enable full PoC persistence and SIEM export of change_event and PoC id manifest.
- Add dashboards: signing latency, PoC backlog, sample rate, per-tenant evidence size.
- Safety: if PoC pipeline > 10s median, fallback to async-signing and throttle delegation UI.
Owners: Carlos, SRE lead.

Phase 2 - broad rollout (6–8 wks)
- Roll to all hosted tenants with default sample rates; enable signing in warm lane.
- Publish ingest mapping to partner SIEMs and provide guidance for enterprise customers to fetch PoC bundles via secure artifact endpoints.
- Migrate RBAC v1 linkage: produce a one-time reconciliation job that emits entitlement_change events for existing roles to create PoC history (low-priority, run during off-peak).

Phase 3 - Dedicated & Private deployments (ongoing)
- Provide on-prem signing adapter that integrates with customer KMS (HSM).
- Provide a deployable evidence-exporter that can push manifests to customer SIEM ingest endpoints.

Migration safety net and rollback strategy:
- Every entitlement_change must be idempotent. If PoC persistence fails, we can revert by issuing a compensating revocation event with note referencing failed PoC id.
- Keep RBAC v1 read adapters for 6 months. Plan rollback path to v1 behavior by toggling delegation-token enforcement flags.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- PoC signing latency median < 300ms (hot path) when sync; 99p < 5s for async fallback.
- PoC backlog zero for 99% tenants; alert if queue depth > 1000 for more than 5 minutes.
- SIEM export success rate > 99.5% per day.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How do we prove delegation chains for multi-hop delegation (A delegates to B delegates to C)? Do we store the full chain in PoC or references only? (tradeoff: atomicity vs size).
- Should PoC include a human-readable justification field persisted in hot tier? (privacy vs auditability)
- Define the canonical permission naming conventions and wildcard semantics for easier SIEM grouping.
- Determine PKI rotation semantics and key compromise playbook (coord with security).

Action items (next 30 days):
- [Maya] implement canonicalization lib + tests (python/go/ts).
- [Evan] prototype async signing worker and failure compensation flow.
- [Carlos] dashboard drafts (signing latency, backlog) + configure alerts.
- [Priya] draft SIEM ingestion guide and sample KQL/DSL queries for common investigations.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working design; comments should call out tradeoffs between forensic completeness and index cost.
- If you are an SRE or infra owner: please review the signing latency and egress implications.
- If you are product or solutions: identify any UX constraints around async signing (how we show pending proofs to customers).

Quick links and references (internal):
- Confluence sketch: CONFLUENCE-SEC-DelegationSketch
- Migration ticket: SEC-2147
- PR for canonicalization lib: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac-v2/pull/421

Changelog (brief):
- 2025-10-08 initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-11-02 added sampling + retention tiers (Carlos)
- 2026-02-14 in_review: clarified PoC atomicity notes and added async signing window guidance (Evan)

End.
